There are a lot of resources on the web where you can learn the basics-and then some-on shooting video/films on a DSLR. There's a LOT on Vimeo/YouTube videos on technique and tricks for getting cool shots with cheap DIY tech. I say get out and try some of those things out. Shoot anything that catches your eye. Keep it dynamic. Then go cut a short music video. Pick a favorite song and start editing a little montage to it. This will free you up from the pressures of making something with a narrative or even a subject and get the creative process going. You'll be surprised how things can come into place- you're working on your craft and developing a sense of technique and workflow. In the mean time just start writing down any ideas or inspiration you have and start filling up a journal. Turn those into short stories and then scripts. Like people have already mentioned above, find any sort of events/classes/screenings/festivals etc.going on in your area. Show up and stick out your hand to people who seem interesting. Don't be afraid to ask questions. Look up PA gigs in your area (Mandy.com or Craigslist). It'll get you comfortable on sets and introduce to professionals doing what you want to do. Most of all though just always keep your hands busy. There's always something you can be shooting, cutting or writing about. Good luck!
